simple.meaning: דְּמִי (dᵉmîy) is a Hebrew word meaning “quiet.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: דְּמִי (H1824) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Psalms 83:2, with occurrences in Psalms, Isaiah.

simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in דְּמִי (H1824) before moving outward to related references.

definitions.full: H1824. domi דֳּמִי noun [masculine] cessation, pause, quiet, rest ; ׳ד Isa 62:6 2 t.; construct דְּמִי 38:10 (but see below); — 1 quiet , in phrase ׳אַלדֿ לָכֶם Isa 62:6 keep not quiet (let there be no quiet to you ); in prayer to God ׳אַלדֿ לָךְ Psa 83:2 keep not quiet (inactive; || שׁקט חרשׂ, ); compare ד ׳וְאַלתִּֿתְּנוּ לוֺ Isa 62:7 and give no rest to him ( ׳י ). 2 in phrase יָמַי בִּדְמִי , apparently quiet, peacefulness , even tenour, of my days (so De Or SS); others, as Hi Ew Che Di, pause, resting-time , i.e. noon-day (compare ᵑ9 ᵑ6 , & height ᵐ5 ), figurative of middle life, but usage dubious; Klo SK 1884, 157 cessation, pause , of natural end of life, Hezekiah's natural expectation, in, contrast with the speedy death implied in v b ; but parallelism of Isa 62:11 a is ag. this; Brd emends בְּרֻם after ᵐ5 ; Klo l.c. suggests בְּתֹם or כְּתֹם as possible, though not necessary; — but view stated first is on the whole best.
